validity.recommendation: no action on existence/classification/duplicate; row is a real, correctly-classified FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transmission pipeline representing Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company's original 1959 mainline
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM, via multiple non-GEM origins. (1) Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company's own corporate site (esng.com/about/our-history/, verified): 'ESNG was incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in 1955... In 1959, ESNG saw the completion of our original pipeline, extending from an interconnect with Transcontinental Gas Pipeline Company (Transco) in Parkesburg, PA, through Delaware and terminating in Salisbury, MD'. (2) FERC's own Environmental Assessment for Docket CP17-28-000 ('2017 Expansion Project Environmental Assessment', Author=FERC, issued 2017-05-12, 295pp, obtained and read in full -- not merely a live URL, the document's own metadata plus body text were inspected via pdftotext): 'Eastern Shore has provided natural gas service to the Delmarva Peninsula and Pennsylvania since 1959. Eastern Shore is an interstate pipeline system operating under the jurisdiction of FERC.' -- this is a genuinely independent federal-regulatory confirmation, distinct from the company's own site, though I could not re-derive a live/re-verifiable URL for this specific 34MB document within this session (Wayback's availability API was rate-limited/timing out on every elibrary.ferc.gov query attempted; see Length note below for the same constraint) -- so it is NOT cited as a proposed_ref below, only reported here as an existence/attribution finding I hand-verified from the document text. (3) Chesapeake Utilities Corporation's own site (chpk.com/about-us/our-businesses/eastern-shore-natural-gas/, verified) independently restates: 'ESNG owns and operates a 517-mile FERC regulated interstate transmission pipeline system that delivers natural gas from four upstream pipeline interconnection points in Pennsylvania and Delaware'. (4) A long, continuous run of Federal Register notices of application/EA-schedule spanning 2013-2023 (2013-15858, 2014-29704, 2015-14739, 2016-03323, 2017-00986, 2017-05308, 2018-21498, 2018-25804, 2023-20456, 2023-28754 -- all verified live), each captioned 'Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company', confirms this is a real, continuously FERC-active interstate pipeline company from at least 2013 through December 2023, not a stale/defunct entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as an operating natural gas interstate transmission pipeline (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission) -- confirmed by both the FERC EA ('interstate pipeline system operating under the jurisdiction of FERC') and Chesapeake's own description ('FERC regulated interstate transmission pipeline system'). DUPLICATE: checked against the 46-row batch roster and against sibling Eastern Shore rows P2003 (2017 Expansion Project, ~40 mi) and P6003 (Del-Mar Energy Pathway Project, ~20 mi). These are NOT duplicates or relabels of P0182 -- they are legitimately separate, later, additive FERC-docketed expansion projects: P2003 corresponds to Docket CP17-28-000 (Federal Register 2017-00986 confirms 'seven segments of buried natural gas pipeline totaling approximately 39.6 miles' in PA/MD/DE, filed Dec 2016), and P6003 corresponds to Docket CP18-548-000 (Federal Register 2018-21498 confirms 4.9+7.39+6.83+0.35 = ~19.5 miles of new loop/extension segments in DE/MD, filed Sept 2018) -- both cleanly distinct from P0182's original 1959 mainline construction. No other row in the 46-row roster plausibly describes this same physical pipe. CAVEATS folded into separate concern entries below: (1) FuelSource is missing a third confirmed upstream interconnect (Texas Eastern Transmission, LP); (2) Location's EndState/Province is very likely wrong (Delaware instead of Maryland, the original mainline's actual terminus) and StartLocation/EndLocation (city-level) are blank and owed; (3) Length (732 km / ~455 mi) could not be pinned to any single documented milestone and is flagged as an unconfirmed spec point; (4) Capacity (100 MMcf/d) likewise could not be independently confirmed.

Tested hard per the batch brief's explicit instruction. Every current-day company source describes Eastern Shore's TOTAL, present-day system (which now includes P2003's 2017 Expansion and P6003's Del-Mar Energy Pathway, plus several untracked expansions -- see cross_row_leads) as either 517 miles (chpk.com, verified) or 532 miles (esng.com/about/our-pipeline-assets/, verified) -- these are SYSTEM-WIDE current totals, not valid refs for a single original-construction segment (aggregate-vs-segment rule). Arithmetic check: 517 mi (current total) - ~40 mi (P2003) - ~20 mi (P6003) = ~457 mi, which is close to but not an exact documented match for 732 km (=454.8 mi) -- suggestive but not a citable equivalence, since it ignores the many OTHER untracked expansions documented on ESNG's own history page and in Federal Register filings (1965 Bridgeville-Cambridge 30 mi, 1981 Dover-Canterbury 8 mi, 2000 Harrington-Milford 8 mi, two multi-year 2000s expansions totaling ~65 mi, 2013 White Oak Lateral 5.5 mi, 2016 White Oak Mainline Expansion, 2023 Worcester Resiliency Upgrade -- none of which are separately tracked as their own GEM rows). Summing ESNG's own history-page mileage additions against a plausible ~1959 starting mileage does not cleanly converge on 454.8 mi either. No single source -- FERC docket, EIA, trade press, or ESNG's own material -- was found stating a distinct '732 km' or '~455 mi' milestone figure for any specific year or construction phase. Concluding this is a genuine, unresolved spec discrepancy rather than staging a fabricated correction or a system-total ref that would violate the aggregate-vs-segment rule. Tier: low/unconfirmed.

cross_row_leads.facts: P2003 (Eastern Shore's '2017 Expansion Project') = FERC Docket CP17-28-000 (pre-filing PF16-7-000). Application filed 2016-12-30; Federal Register notice of application 2017-01-18 (2017-00986); 'seven segments of buried natural gas pipeline totaling approximately 39.6 miles' in Chester County PA, Cecil County MD, and New Castle/Sussex Counties DE, plus 3,750 hp added at the Daleville Compressor Station; total project cost ~$98,578,673; ESNG's own history page states this expansion was 'completed in 2020' and 'added approximately 40 miles of pipeline'; diameters per the EA/notice are a mix of 10-, 16-, and 24-inch loop segments plus a separate 10-inch 16.9-mile mainline extension.

P6003 (Eastern Shore's 'Del-Mar Energy Pathway Project') = FERC Docket CP18-548-000. Application filed 2018-09-14; comprises (i) ~4.9 mi of 16-inch loop in Kent County, DE; (ii) ~7.39 mi of 8-inch mainline extension in Sussex County, DE; (iii) ~6.83 mi of 10-inch mainline extension in Wicomico and Somerset Counties, MD; (iv) ~0.35 mi of 10-inch mainline extension (pressure-control upgrade) in Sussex County, DE -- totaling ~19.5 mi, consistent with GEM's recorded ~20 mi for this row; brought gas service to Somerset County, MD for the first time per ESNG's own history page.

summary: P0182 Eastern Shore (original 1959 mainline): existence/classification/duplicate all confirmed clean via ESNG/Chesapeake's own sites, a fully-read FERC EA (CP17-28-000), and 10 Federal Register notices spanning 2013-2023; 3 concerns staged -- FuelSource missing Texas Eastern Transmission LP (high tier, 2 independent origins), EndState likely wrong (Delaware -> Maryland; the mainline terminates in Salisbury MD, not DE) with StartLocation/EndLocation now filled, and Length (732 km) plus Capacity (100 MMcf/d) both left as unconfirmed spec points after hard testing (no source ties either figure to a specific milestone; only aggregate current-system totals of 517-532 mi / ~295-300k dekatherms/day were found, correctly rejected as segment-vs-aggregate mismatches). 8 units refs-added (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Start, FuelSource, Location, Operator, Owner); 7 left UNRESOLVED (Proposal, Construction, Capacity, Pressure, Length, Diameter, SegmentCost) after documented targeted searches, mostly attributable to this row representing 1959-vintage construction predating FERC's digital docket era. Two untracked sibling expansion projects (P2003=CP17-28-000, P6003=CP18-548-000) confirmed as genuinely separate, non-duplicate rows and detailed in cross_row_leads.
